newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Court to review ex-bodyguard's case vs Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Court to review ex-bodyguard's case vs Yeltsin.

text.p: A Russian court will resume its hearing on Monday of a case brought against President Boris Yeltsin by his former bodyguard Alexander Korzhakov, Interfax news agency reported.
The burly 46-year-old former KGB officer claims Yeltsin defamed him in a written order dismissing him from the armed forces late last month.
Interfax quoted Lidya Sorokina, judge for the case at the Kuntsevo municipal court in Moscow, as saying that neither side had turned up or sent representatives for the first hearing on November 11.

Sorokina said the presidential administration had sent a letter saying the court order had arrived too late for it to send a representative to the first hearing. Korzhakov had not chosen his lawyer at that stage, she added.
Korzhakov's petition demanded that Yeltsin, currently in hospital recovering from a heart operation, take back allegations made in an order dismissing him from the armed forces, Interfax said.

"After his sacking on June 20, 1996, Lieutenant-General Alexander Korzhakov has come out with a series of lies concerning the Russian president and members of his family," said the order, read by Yeltsin's spokesman on October 28.

"He has allowed himself to publish confidential information he obtained in office. Korzhakov's public threats to disclose information that he possesses are aimed at discrediting top state officials," it said.
Korzhakov was a close friend of the Yeltsin family until his sacking in June.
He is now at odds with Yeltsin and his chief of staff Anatoly Chubais and has formed a political partnership with the ousted former national security adviser Alexander Lebed.
Korzhakov is now embroiled in a new scandal with Chubais, who played a key part in his dimissal and has boosted his own power during Yeltsin's illness.
The Moscow daily Moskovsky Komsomolets published a transcript it hinted had come from Korzhakov suggesting wrongdoings in the financing of Yeltsin's campaign for re-election.
Both Chubais and Korzhakov denied having anything to do with the transcript.
